# BitChord 1.0.8
## Playback
- Fixes "Couldn't open a stream for that track" and "confirm you're not a bot" on networks where other YouTube clients still play. BitChord kept presenting the same YouTube identity once it had been flagged, so no retry, network or account could clear it. Each track is now asked for with a fresh anonymous identity, the way the working clients ask, and YouTube cookies are no longer stored. - The YouTube extractor is updated to InnerTubeX 0.11.6. - A track that fails is no longer asked for again in quick bursts, which could make a flagged network worse. - Diagnostic reports now say which YouTube client refused a track and why.
## Security
- rustls 0.23.46.

# BitChord 1.0.7
## Automix
- Transitions are calmer on the CPU. Track analysis is paced so it no longer piles up with playback resolution, and each track is decoded once for analysis. - Less memory during transitions. The Neural Engine beat model has a new version (v2) that holds about 370 MB less, and it is released shortly after use instead of lingering. Peaks drop from about 1.1 GB to about 700 MB. - Installed Automix models update themselves when a newer version is pinned; the old one keeps working until the new one is verified. With Wi-Fi-only downloads on, a metered connection still waits for Wi-Fi.
## Lyrics
- Untimed lyrics are aligned against the whole song, including songs in several languages and scripts without spaces. - Lyrics on Player can be turned off in Settings.
## Playback
- Songs start faster after launch: the prepared YouTube player is cached on disk. - The playing-row bars and the title marquee use far less CPU, especially on Mac.

# BitChord 1.0.6
## Now Playing
- A title too long for the player no longer widens it. On iPhone the player stayed pushed past the right edge, and on Mac the title spilled past the left. Long titles now stay in their column and scroll.
## Updates
- Release notes now cover every version you skipped. The update sheet lists each release between your version and the latest, newest first, and the first launch after an update shows what changed since the version you last ran. - Release notes are formatted: headings, lists, bold text, links and commands display properly instead of as raw Markdown. - **Mac:** **Check for Updates…** is in the BitChord menu.
